tip: 도둑이 제 발 저리다 (dodugi je bal jeorida) = the guilty give themselves away.
세 살 버릇 여든까지 간다 (se sal beoreut yeodeunkkaji ganda) = childhood habits last for life.
백문이 불여일견 (baengmuni buryeoilgyeon, 百聞不如一見) = seeing for yourself beats hearsay.
The frame 것은 ... 때문이다 (geoseun ... ttaemunida) means 'the reason X is Y': 지켰던 것은 (jikyeotdeon geoseun) sets up the fact, 때문이다 gives the cause.
-(으)며 links simultaneous actions: 걸으며 (georeumyeo = while walking).
-는데도 = even though: 줬는데도 (jwonneundedo = even though I warned).
The -(으)ㅁ (-eum) ending turns a whole clause into a formal noun: 일어설 수 있음 (ireoseol su isseum) = 'being able to stand back up'. Written style packs ideas into nouns.
Korean puts the whole describing clause before its noun: 겨우 탄 비행기 (gyeou tan bihaenggi) = the 'barely-boarded' plane. English trails with 'that I barely boarded'; Korean front-loads it.
-기를 아까워하다 = begrudge doing: 쓰기를 아까워하다 (sseugireul akkawohada = begrudge spending).
것이야말로 = this very thing: 잃지 않는 것이야말로 (ilchi anneun geosiyamallo = precisely not losing it).
-기는커녕 = so far from it that the opposite happened: 쉬기는커녕 (swigineun-keonyeong = far from resting).
-고 나서야 = not until: 돌아가시고 나서야 (doragasigo naseoya = only after he passed).
The -은 word sets the topic and the -이 word narrows it: 팀장님은 결정이 빠르다 (timjangnimeun gyeoljeongi ppareuda = as for the lead, decisions are fast).
것이다 caps a claim: 허물어진다는 것이다 (heomureojindaneun geosida = the point is it collapses).
-았/었더라면 = if it had been otherwise: 없었더라면 (eopseotdeoramyeon = had there not been).
것이다 asserts a judgment: 외면하는 것이다 (oemyeonhaneun geosida = they turn a blind eye).
-(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 = no way it could: 알 리가 없었다 (al riga eopseotda = there was no way to know).
-(으)며 (-myeo) is the written cousin of spoken -(으)면서 (-myeonseo = while): 가로지르며 (garojireumyeo) = while crossing. Writing leans -며, speech leans -면서.
-은/는커녕 flips the expectation: 공감은커녕 (gonggameun-keonyeong = far from empathizing).
-(으)ㄹ 만큼 = to the extent: 알아들었을 만큼 (aradeureosseul mankeum = enough to understand).
-고 나서 (-go naseo) alone means 'after' – the extra 야 (ya) sharpens it to 'only after': 옮기고 나서야 (omgigo naseoya) = only after I transferred.
-곤 하다 = recurring habit: 힘들어지곤 한다 (himdeureojigon handa = tends to become hard).
-는 것보다 compares acts: 해결하는 것보다 (haegyeolhaneun geotboda = than solving it).
-ㄴ/는다는 것은 defines an act: 쓴다는 것은 (sseundaneun geoseun = the act of writing is).
-기 때문이다 states the cause: 사라지기 때문일 것이다 (sarajigi ttaemunil geosida = probably because it vanishes).
-ㄴ/는다 해도 = even granting: 발전한다 해도 (baljeonhanda haedo = even if it advances).
-(으)ㄴ 김에 = while you're at it: 내려간 김에 (naeryeogan gime = since I was back home).
-기보다 = rather than: 있다기보다 (itdagiboda = rather than lying in).
-기란 (-giran) sets up 'as for doing X' and expects an easy/hard verdict: 두려워하지 않기란 (duryeowohaji ankiran) = as for not fearing... (no easy thing).
-(으)ㄹ수록 = the more, the more: 친구 사이일수록 (chingu saiilsurok = the longer you've been friends).
